gap: No result ChatGPT got states that when The Technology Man (Gidon, 2024-06-20) tested the HOTO precision driver with a digital torque screwdriver, both gears read between 0.1 and 0.2 N·m. That means the gear HOTO rates at 0.05 N·m measured at least twice its rating. No result sets that beside Fanttik's own bench test, which put the E1 Max's 0.2 N·m setting at 0.192–0.208 N·m over the 5 runs it published.
standout_why: The cited rivals have no measured figures. fanttik.com 'HOTO vs Fanttik' gives only Fanttik's ratings, calls them 'verified' without saying who verified them, and gives no HOTO figures. I could not load the cited Fanttik E1 Max product page (HTTP 429). Among the uncited results, toolengineers.com says 'We did not perform original torque calibration, screw-cycle, battery-runtime, or bit-wear testing', butactuallygood.com says 'nothing below is a physical test result', and our own Dealectric page cites only maker figures. One uncited result, legitproductreviews.com (rank 4 in chat r2), does pass on The Technology Man's 170 rpm and '0.1 to 0.2 Nm', which is why this scores 1 and not 2. It does not point out that the low gear measured at least double its 0.05 N·m rating, and it has no Fanttik bench spread. No result ChatGPT got has an independent torque or rpm measurement for either Fanttik model, the iFixit or the Ryobi.
decides: This supports picking the Fanttik E1 Max for delicate work, but it does not settle it. The only measured low-gear figure for the HOTO says its 'gentle' 0.05 N·m setting delivers 0.1–0.2 N·m, close to the high setting. Its 170 rpm rating did hold up under a tachometer. The E1 Max's accuracy figure comes only from Fanttik, so the page can present it as a maker claim with numbers attached, not as independent proof. Its low 0.05 N·m gear has no measurement from anyone.

findings.product: HOTO Electric Precision Screwdriver Kit Pro
findings.label: Torque measured on both electric gears (rated 0.05 and 0.2 N·m)
findings.value: 0.1–0.2 N·m on both gears, always under 0.3 N·m
findings.source_title: HOTO Electric Precision Screwdriver Pro Kit Review vs iFixit – Gadget of the Week Ep03 (The Technology Man)
findings.note: Gidon, The Technology Man, posted 20 June 2024: 'I measured both gears with a digital torque screwdriver and got between 0.1NM and 0.2NM and always less than 0.3NM.' Because both gears fall in that range, the low gear rated 0.05 N·m read at least 0.1 N·m, 2× or more its rating. He gives no run count or per-gear split. Tested the Kit Pro (48-piece). Our page lists the ADV, which HOTO and retailers also rate at 170 RPM and 0.05/0.2 N·m. That the two use the same driver is my inference from the matching specs, not confirmed.

findings.value: 0.192–0.208 N·m over 5 published runs, mean 0.2008 N·m (+0.4%)
findings.source_title: Decoding Torque Accuracy Ratings for Cordless Drivers (Fanttik)
findings.note: Fanttik Official, published 2026-01-16. Digital torque tester calibrated for 0.1–5.0 N·m. The article says '10 consecutive runs' but lists only 5: 0.198, 0.205, 0.201, 0.192, 0.208 N·m. Spread 0.016 N·m, worst run ±4%. Fanttik calls the result 'representative'. The 0.05 N·m low gear is below the tester's calibrated range and was not reported.
